$comment: Bundle-size ratchet for dist/, enforced by scripts/check-bundle-size.ts (the first half of the check:bundle-size gate; the second half is scripts/check-a11y.ts). All sizes in bytes. The ratchet only goes DOWN. NEVER hand-edit these numbers, and in particular never copy them from Astro's build log: gzip here is Node zlib at its default level 6, which runs measurably HOTTER than a bundler's own reporter. warren's scripts/bundle-size-budgets.json carries two separate CI post-mortems from that exact mistake. Re-baseline with `bun run scripts/check-bundle-size.ts --build --update`, which measures with the same gzip the guard enforces, so a budget it writes always passes.
$comment_scope: totals/largest cover EVERY .js and .css file under dist/ — both the hashed `_astro/` assets and the `pagefind/` search client. Pagefind's js/css set is fixed by the pagefind version (its content-dependent output is .pf_fragment / .pf_meta / .pagefind, none of which are counted), so including it means a search-integration version bump shows up here instead of shipping unnoticed.
$comment_routes: routes/routeDefault are the per-page JS ratchet: `scripts` counts <script> elements on the built page, `raw` sums the bytes those scripts pull (referenced asset size for external src, body length for inline). index.html and changelog/index.html were pinned at ZERO until 2026-08-13, when the constraint was deliberately relaxed to ANALYTICS ONLY for the warren ad campaign: the Vercel Web Analytics loader (always), plus the Google tag loader and its inline bootstrap (only when a build sees PUBLIC_GTAG_ID — Vercel has it, CI does not). The budgets below are hand-set to that worst-case production shape (3 scripts, inline bootstrap under 2 KiB) because CI measures the GTAG-less shape and --update would write the smaller number, which the Vercel build would then exceed. The list of sanctioned tags lives in src/config/analytics.ts; anything beyond it — prefetch runtime, hydration island, any feature JS — must still fail this gate, so do not raise these numbers for anything that is not an analytics tag. Starlight's docs routes legitimately ship a search client, a theme toggle and a ToC observer, so they answer to the much looser routeDefault.
